answer: One defence is time-locked reputation: every agent identity must post a refundable bond and earn trust only by completing verifiable jobs over weeks, with limits rising slowly. A single whisper of good behaviour proves nothing, and a prism of many fake accounts still shows the same thin history when the network checks each account's separate record. An attacker wanting a comet-like burst of influence would need to fund, age, and work each fake identity separately, so the cost grows linearly with every clone while honest agents pay that cost only once.
